findings.title: Blocked-email match is case-sensitive and does not trim
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? loads a row with an exact where(email: email) comparison, and nothing downcases or strips the address on write or lookup. Uniqueness is case-sensitive, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive, so User@spam.com and user@spam.com can both be stored and only one of them matches. Signup assigns params[:email] unchanged (User.new_from_params) and EmailValidator passes that raw value in. Elsewhere this app treats addresses as case-insensitive: UsersController#change_email uses Email.downcase(...).strip, and the domain regexp is built ignore-case. A listed address can therefore be used to register by changing case or adding surrounding whitespace, so the block list does not stop the signup it is meant to stop. Normalize with the same downcase-and-strip helper on save and in should_block?, and enforce a case-insensitive unique index.

findings.title: Match stats are written during validation and counted twice per signup
findings.body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block? from validate_each, but should_block? is not a pure check: on any hit it increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and save the row, including when action_type is do_nothing (the method returns false and no error is added). UsersController#create calls user.valid? at line 168 and then user.save at line 172, and save runs validations again. One signup attempt against a screened address therefore records two matches. The same write runs for every other valid? or failed save, including attempts that never create a user. match_count and last_match_at, which the model spec treats as the record of how often an address was seen, will be inflated, and every anonymous signup POST that hits a screened address performs a database write as a side effect of validation. Record the match once, after a real attempt, with an atomic update outside the validator.

findings.title: match_count update is a lost-update read-modify-write
findings.body: should_block? loads match_count, adds 1 in Ruby, and save writes that absolute value back. Two concurrent requests that both read the same count will both persist count+1, so attempts are dropped. save also runs validations and callbacks and writes every dirty column, so a failure or delay on this row can turn a signup validation into an error, or overwrite a concurrent last_match_at. Increment with an atomic update (update_counters or increment_counter) and set last_match_at with update_column so concurrent matches are not lost and other columns are not rewritten.

findings.title: Domain allow/deny regexp is unanchored and barely escaped
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? interpolates the site setting into a regexp of the form @(domain-list) after escaping only dots, then matches with =~, which succeeds on any substring and is not anchored at the end of the address. A whitelist entry of company.com therefore accepts attacker@company.com.evil.com. A blacklist entry of spam.com does not match user@mail.spam.com, because the character before spam.com is a dot rather than @, so subdomain addresses bypass the blacklist. Other regexp metacharacters in the setting are not escaped, so an invalid fragment raises RegexpError during validation and registration returns 500 instead of a validation error. This is the domain check moved from User, and it is still wrong. Anchor the host to the end of the string, decide explicitly whether subdomains should match, and escape metacharacters before interpolation.

findings.title: Specs miss case bypass, double-count, and domain rules
findings.body: EmailValidator specs stub BlockedEmail.should_block? and never create a blocked row, and BlockedEmail specs only call should_block? with the exact stored string. Nothing asserts that User validation (validates :email, email: true) rejects a blocked address, that a case or whitespace variant is blocked, that UsersController#create increments match_count once, or that the whitelist/blacklist branches accept or reject the suffix and subdomain cases above. Those bugs would leave this suite green.
